summary: Built the three Business Hours calendars and a 12-month holiday seed set as one Settings:BusinessHours file, plus the Q90 holiday-maintenance runbook, the package.xml fragment at version 67.0 and a deploy-order note. check-outputs returned ok on all three declared outputs. The step ends BLOCKED, not built: the cited skill's checker — the one this step's acceptance_tests[0] declares with expected exit 0 — rejects the 'Severity 1 24x7' calendar because all seven days are 00:00:00.000Z to 00:00:00.000Z, which is the shipped-24/7 shape its rule exists to catch. That shape is the only one the skill documents for an always-open calendar, and the requirement (L18, 'Severity 1 outages are 24/7 and never pause') is what asked for it, so the artefact is correct and the rule cannot tell a deliberate always-open calendar from a neglected default. Both available repairs were tested on scratch copies and both rejected on grounding: deleting the calendar overrules the plan's own inputs and manual test, and trimming it to Mon-Fri passes the checker while silently closing the never-pausing calendar at weekends. A third, inventing a 23:59:59-style end value, is the class of guess that forced the M3 rebuild. The decision is a human's: amend the plan to carry the 24/7 promise on M4-S04's businessHoursSource=None entry as its own note already specifies, or change the checker rule so a non-default always-open calendar is INFO rather than ISSUE.

refusal.message: check_business_hours_and_holidays.py rejects the 'Severity 1 24x7' calendar with: "every day is 00:00:00.000Z to 00:00:00.000Z - this is the shipped 24/7 shape; SLA clocks on this calendar never pause." The artefact is correct per the skill's own reference (gotchas #1: the shipped Default 24/7 calendar stores exactly this pair and 'the same pair of values means open the whole day'), and the calendar was required by steps[M4-S01].inputs.calendars and by acceptance_tests[3]. Passing the gate would require either deleting a plan-mandated calendar, closing a never-pausing calendar at weekends, or inventing an undocumented time value. Per agents/metadata-builder/AGENT.md, a checker that rejects an artefact this agent believes correct is REFUSAL_NEEDS_HUMAN_REVIEW, not a repair loop: three passes cannot fix what is not in the XML.
refusal.remediation_hint: Pick one: (1) build_plan.py amend-step M4-S01 to drop 'Severity 1 24x7' from inputs.calendars and acceptance_tests[3], leaving the 24/7 promise to M4-S04's businessHoursSource=None entry, which steps[M4-S04].inputs.note already specifies and which skills/admin/business-hours-and-holidays SKILL.md Decision Guidance names as the mechanism; or (2) change the checker rule so an always-open calendar that is not the org default is INFO rather than ISSUE, the same shape as the M2 finding resolved in commit 214da9abd. Option 1 costs a future Severity 1 entitlement process, which has no None source and reads the process calendar (gotchas #5).

process_observations.observation: Every element written is present in the skill's retrieved worked example: the businessHours child order, the HH:mm:ss.SSSZ day windows, the repeated <businessHours> attachment on a holiday, and the startTime/endTime pair for a partial-day close were all copied rather than recalled.

The weekend days are absent from both regional calendars rather than written as midnight-to-midnight pairs, which is what the skill's example explicitly instructs and what keeps them out of the checker's all_midnight rule.

This step's acceptance_tests[0] description enumerates three of the checker's rules ('exactly one default calendar, no calendar with an empty week, and no holiday already in the past') and does not mention the all-midnight rule that the step's own third calendar necessarily trips, so the conflict was invisible at plan-verification time.

No step in M4 reads a 'Severity 1 24x7' calendar: M4-S02 builds Premier and Standard processes only, M4-S03 stamps Case.BusinessHoursId from Account.Region__c which yields EMEA or US, and M4-S04's Severity 1 entry is specified with businessHoursSource None, which reads no calendar at all.

Trimming the always-open calendar to Monday-Friday makes the checker exit 0 while leaving a calendar that claims to never pause and is closed every weekend; the gate cannot see the difference, which makes this the cheapest wrong fix available to a later run.

Acme's holiday list was never asked for: Q39 settled that each region has its own set and no question, answer key row or requirement line names a single date, so the 14 entries written are a seeded 12-month set marked UNCONFIRMED rather than a customer artefact.

The skill documents isRecurring, recurrenceStartDate and recurrenceEndDate but no element stating how often a holiday recurs, so every entry was written in the fully documented one-off form with an explicit activityDate instead of asserting a recurrence the file cannot express.

Q90 named the accountable team (Service Operations) and the cadence (a Q4 yearly deploy) but not the individual, so the runbook carries the owner row as OPEN for the M4 gate rather than inventing a name.
Once the checker-policy decision is made and this step is rebuilt, the step's four acceptance tests still have to be run by their owner rather than inferred from this run.
